explanation: Exception is a checked exception, not a RuntimeException subclass; the second catch block handles it and prints 'Caught Exception'.
finally block always executes; it runs before the return statement takes effect, then the value 10 is returned (After never executes).
ArithmeticException is caught, prints 'Caught', then finally block executes and prints 'Finally'.
parseInt('abc') throws NumberFormatException, caught by the first catch block (more specific), so 'Number Error' is printed.
null + 1 attempts autoboxing and arithmetic on null, triggering a NullPointerException, caught and prints 'NPE'.
A method can declare throws IOException even if it doesn't actually throw it; the declaration is a contract, not a guarantee.
finally block throws RuntimeException, which suppresses the original IllegalArgumentException; RuntimeException is what propagates.
x is set to 20, then 30 in catch, then 40 in finally (which always executes last), so final value is 40.
Try-with-resources (Java 7+) automatically closes the Scanner resource after the try block, no finally needed.
Exception (not RuntimeException) is thrown, not caught by catch, but finally still executes; After is skipped as exception propagates.
